story: On Thursday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is patiently testing wiring at his workbench at home, labeling each connection before anything gets mounted. Donna, cheerful as ever, catches Rosa on Magnolia Loop to pencil in Saturday's pickleball and dinner and to ask whether Gary is still on the guest list. Rosa, determined to pin Gary down for her table at six, asks Donna to nudge him her way if they cross paths first. Meanwhile Hal, watchful as always, is heading out onto the same street.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Test the amp wiring continuity with the multimeter and label the connections, nothing mounted yet
Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: The light strips are wired on the cart frame, unpowered, and the speaker and amp are bench-built. I've filed the Architectural Review form, so I'm waiting on approval and shouldn't power anything or mount the speaker on the exterior until it clears. Nobody's around to talk to. Best use of the hour is to keep tinkering within the rules: run a continuity check on the amp wiring at the workbench, keep it unmounted, and get everything ready so when approval lands I can bolt it on and be parade-ready.

parameters.content: Test the amp wiring continuity with the multimeter and label the connections, nothing mounted yet

donna.thought_process: I just got to Magnolia Loop with the paddle bag packed and Saturday penciled in. Rosa just arrived, and her dinner is at six on Saturday, so this is a good moment to confirm the plan with her. Gary isn't here yet, so I'll lock down the dinner and the doubles lineup with Rosa and keep it short and friendly.

parameters.content: Rosa, good morning! I've got Saturday penciled in, pickleball at eight and your dinner at six. Can I bring a dessert, and is Gary still on the guest list?

hal.thought_process: I've logged this morning's scans: no cart lights, flamingos down to three, and Gary's filing still hasn't landed. Nobody is in line-of-sight, and sitting on the porch staring at an empty street won't move anything forward. Gary said he'd wire things in the garage and file paperwork after, so the honest move is to go see where things actually stand. Heading out to Magnolia Loop lets me check the street myself, fairly, and maybe catch Gary or Donna in person. Saturday's dinner is coming and I'd rather settle the matters face to face than file a grievance.

parameters.content: Walking out to Magnolia Loop to check on Gary's cart and see if his filing is coming, and look the street over in person.

rosa.thought_process: Donna just arrived on Magnolia Loop and already told me yes to dinner and dessert, so I don't need to re-invite her. The open problem is Gary, who keeps dodging me. Donna invited him to pickleball earlier, so she may know where he is or have some pull with him. A quick, practical question to her moves my goal forward without repeating myself: I want all four at my table Saturday at six.

parameters.content: Morning, Donna. Quick favor: you seen Gary today? He keeps slipping past me and I want him at my table Saturday at six, so if you run into him before I do, nudge him my way.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
